scenes.headline: 400 Horsepower
scenes.narration: With 400 horsepower and a design that's instantly iconic, this one from 1996 stands out as a symbol of high-performance engineering.

scenes.headline: First-AWD Turbo
scenes.narration: This was the first 911 Turbo to feature all-wheel drive, enhancing its traction and stability across various driving conditions.

scenes.headline: Aerodynamic Design
scenes.narration: The distinct whale tail rear spoiler not only defines its look but significantly aids aerodynamics, crucial for high-speed stability.

scenes.headline: Classic Cockpit
scenes.narration: Inside, the traditional layout features the Porsche's classic gauge cluster with a central tachometer, emphasizing driver focus.

scenes.headline: Value
scenes.narration: Originally priced at around $110,000, these models now trade for about $70,000, reflecting strong enthusiast demand over time.

scenes.headline: Air-Cooled Icon
scenes.narration: The 993 Turbo remains an icon as Porsche's last air-cooled Turbo, renowned for its pure driving experience and engineering excellence.

scenes.headline: Iconic Reputation
scenes.narration: Known for its powerful performance and distinct styling, the 993 has cemented itself as a classic, beloved by enthusiasts worldwide.
With its enduring style and formidable power, would you take this classic 911 Turbo for a spin, or is its iconic appeal not quite your style?

script: With 400 horsepower and a design that's instantly iconic, this one from 1996 stands out as a symbol of high-performance engineering. This was the first 911 Turbo to feature all-wheel drive, enhancing its traction and stability across various driving conditions. The distinct whale tail rear spoiler not only defines its look but significantly aids aerodynamics, crucial for high-speed stability. Inside, the traditional layout features the Porsche's classic gauge cluster with a central tachometer, emphasizing driver focus. Originally priced at around $110,000, these models now trade for about $70,000, reflecting strong enthusiast demand over time. The 993 Turbo remains an icon as Porsche's last air-cooled Turbo, renowned for its pure driving experience and engineering excellence. Known for its powerful performance and distinct styling, the 993 has cemented itself as a classic, beloved by enthusiasts worldwide. With its enduring style and formidable power, would you take this classic 911 Turbo for a spin, or is its iconic appeal not quite your style?

sections.Highlights: THIS… is a 1996 Porsche 911 Turbo, finished in Arena Red Metallic with a black interior. This 911 Turbo is owned by journalist and Cars & Bids founder Doug DeMuro, and associated videos are viewable below. This Porsche is equipped with a 6-speed manual transmission, and the odometer currently displays approximately 62,800 miles. This 993 is offered with a clean Carfax vehicle history report, and it has reportedly been registered in California since new. According to the window sticker provided in the gallery, notable factory equipment includes 18-inch Turbo Twist wheels, a limited-slip differential, a sunroof, supple leather upholstery, power-adjustable front seats, and air conditioning. Notable modifications reported by the seller are limited to a Porsche Classic Communication Management (PCCM) head unit. Documentation of maintenance and repairs performed is extensive and reportedly dates back to new. Recent highlights include a $24,470 service in February 2026 that included replacing the valve covers, timing chain covers, crankshaft seal, turbo oil feed lines, and more, as detailed by documentation in the gallery. The 993-generation 911 Turbo, introduced in 1995, was the first 911 Turbo with all-wheel drive, providing enhanced traction and stability. Its twin-turbocharged flat-6 engine, distinctive wide-body design, and status as the final air-cooled Porsche have made it a favorite among Porsche enthusiasts -- and Arena Red Metallic remains one of the most famous 993 Turbo colors thanks to the iconic "Kills Bugs Fast" advertisement. Power comes from a 3.6-liter twin-turbocharged flat-6, rated at 400 horsepower and 398 lb-ft of torque. Power is sent to all four wheels via a 6-speed manual transmission.
sections.Equipment: A window sticker is provided in the photo gallery, and a partial list of notable equipment reported by the seller includes: 18-inch Turbo Twist wheels Xenon headlights Power-operated sunroof Rear wiper Supple leather upholstery Power-adjustable front seats Air conditioning Cruise control
sections.Seller Notes: The seller reports that some touch-up paintwork has been performed on forward-facing surfaces at some point in the past, and a full-body paint protection film and a ceramic coating have since been applied to this 911 Turbo.
